note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, hour, price and schedule below comes from the City of Boulder's own pages: the Racket Sports page for the outdoor court table and the reservation rules, the pickleball page for the indoor and outdoor drop-in schedules, the Racket Sports FAQs for the fee history, and each location's own page for the address, the hours and the amenities. Where the City is silent, on surface, on lighting and on when the courts are busy, this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
Boulder answers parking at four of its five venues. The pages for the North Boulder, East Boulder and South Boulder recreation centres each carry the word "Parking" answered "Yes" under an ADA Accessibility heading, beside restrooms, sidewalks and drinking fountains. That is the whole statement: no lot size, no fee, no time limit.

Chautauqua Park is the one place the City writes a paragraph. Its page is headed "Paid Parking in effect Memorial weekend to Labor Day", with paid parking "on summer weekends and holidays at Chautauqua and nearby neighborhood streets" and a Park-to-Park service that "provides free satellite parking and shuttle service". A summer Saturday game there means paying to park or riding a shuttle.

Foothills Community Park publishes nothing about parking. Restrooms are stated at all five venues.
slots.peak_hours: Boulder does not say when its courts are busy, but it publishes something better: a written drop-in schedule for both indoor and outdoor courts, and a reservation system whose rules are spelled out. Outdoors, the City sets aside "8:30 to 11:30 am on 6 outdoor courts" at South Boulder daily, and at North Boulder "7:30 to 10:30 am on 4 outdoor courts" on Tuesdays and Thursdays plus "6 to 9 pm on 4 outdoor courts" on Wednesdays and Fridays. Those are the only outdoor sessions the City schedules; East Boulder, Chautauqua and Foothills have none. Indoors, three courts go up in each recreation centre gymnasium at fixed times: Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings at North Boulder, Monday afternoon and evening and Sunday afternoon at East Boulder, and Sunday morning plus Tuesday and Thursday afternoons at South Boulder, with the City's footnote that there is no indoor pickleball at South Boulder from June through October. Outside those windows the outdoor courts are "first come and free to all park visitors", or reservable at $10 an hour, up to 7.5 days ahead - "181 rolling hours" in the City's phrase - for a maximum of two hours a day, at least an hour in advance, and with no refunds for weather. The City's own figures suggest reserving is the exception: in 2024, 59% of renters booked only once or twice all year, and fewer than 1% booked twice a week or more. Foothills runs on a different clock. Its four courts exist from 7 a.m. to noon, seven days a week, and after noon the rink goes back to inline hockey and general use. The City adds that drop-in programming is adjusted every six months, in January and July, so the windows above have a shelf life.
slots.surface_condition: The City names no surface for any pickleball court in Boulder. What it names is what they are drawn on. "Pickleball play is on tennis courts with pickleball lines", says the Racket Sports page, "Except for Foothills Community Park which is a designated inline hockey rink." So the twenty outdoor courts are lines on something else: sixteen on tennis courts, four on a hockey rink. The nine indoor courts are on basketball gymnasium floors at drop-in times only, because "pickleball nets are not available outside listed drop-in hours". The table's nets column reads "Rolling" on every row, and the rule is stated: "Pickleball nets should be rolled off tennis courts after completion of play and when not in use." At Foothills there are none to roll: "Please bring your own portable pickleball nets. Nets are not available onsite." Condition is addressed once. The City's FAQ says its planned new courts are part of a plan "while also ensuring we address the poor condition of courts across the system", and when this was read South Boulder's eight outdoor courts were shut under a notice reading "Aug. 17 - tentatively scheduled to reopen Sept. 11: All SBRC Outdoor Racket Courts closed for court resurfacing and restriping." The closure publishes as printed. Lighting is not stated for any venue: "Lights are not guaranteed for use of courts after sunset" is a rule about expectations, not a lighting answer, and the only light timers it mentions are near Tennis Court 1 at North Boulder.
slots.local_scene: Twenty-nine verified courts across five venues - twenty outdoor and nine indoor - and every one of the five is free to play, on the City's own sentence, "Courts are first come and free to all park visitors, a reserved court is available to secure your date and time". Boulder is the first Colorado city on this site. It is one of seven cities on this site with a verified free court, and, with Cape Coral, one of only two where every published venue is free. It is also one of the few operators on this site that publishes a written drop-in schedule for both its indoor and its outdoor courts. North Boulder, East Boulder and South Boulder each have three indoor courts in the gymnasium at drop-in times, "included with your daily entry fee or pass", with four, two and eight outdoor courts beside them. Chautauqua Park has two courts on one tennis court. Foothills Community Park has four on an inline hockey rink, mornings only. The City runs beginner and intermediate classes for ages 16 and up, lessons at all three recreation centres, and a seasonal adult league: two play at once, three-person rosters, one match a night for up to an hour, seven weeks ending in a best-match tournament, at South Boulder or North Boulder. Two sites are named here and not listed. Tom Watson Park appears on the Racket Sports page only under "Additional Tennis Courts" with the figure 4, a tennis count; the City states no pickleball number for it, and the imported dataset's twelve pickleball courts there are an imported number, not a stated one. The FAQ says new courts open there in spring 2026, so it may publish later. East Boulder Community Park - a separate site from the East Boulder Community Center, which does publish - appears only as a lighting note and a project link, with courts planned for spring 2027 and no count. Reservation fees doubled from $5 to $10 an hour on November 14, 2025, the first increase since 2012, the day reservations stopped being included in recreation memberships.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts in one place
best_for.text: South Boulder Recreation Center has eleven courts, the largest set in Boulder: eight outdoor on the tennis courts with pickleball lines, and three indoor in the gymnasium on Sunday mornings and Tuesday and Thursday afternoons outside June to October. The City runs outdoor drop-in here every day, 8:30 to 11:30 am on six courts. The outdoor courts were closed for resurfacing when read, tentatively reopening September 11.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to play after work
best_for.text: North Boulder Recreation Center is the one venue where the City schedules an evening session outdoors: Wednesdays and Fridays, 6 to 9 pm, on four courts, plus Tuesday and Thursday mornings. Three indoor courts run Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings with the daily entry fee or a pass. The City places complimentary light timers near Tennis Court 1 here, while stating that lights are not guaranteed after sunset.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the longest published hours
best_for.text: Chautauqua Park is open 5:00 am to 11:00 pm daily, the longest stated hours of any Boulder venue, with two pickleball courts on a single tennis court - a game rather than a rotation. It is free and first come; reservations cost $10 an hour. The City states paid parking at and near the park on summer weekends and holidays, with a free satellite lot and shuttle through Park-to-Park.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Boulder have?
faqs.a: We have verified 29 across five City venues: eleven at South Boulder Recreation Center, seven at North Boulder Recreation Center, five at East Boulder Community Center, four at Foothills Community Park and two at Chautauqua Park. Twenty are outdoor, from the City's Racket Sports table, and nine are indoor, from the pickleball page's drop-in lines - three in each recreation centre gymnasium at scheduled times.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Boulder?
faqs.a: Yes at all five venues, in the City's own words: "Courts are first come and free to all park visitors, a reserved court is available to secure your date and time." Reserving a court costs $10 an hour, up from $5 on November 14, 2025. Indoor drop-in sessions are included with the recreation centre's daily entry fee or pass, so the indoor courts cost whatever the door costs.

faqs.q: Why is Tom Watson Park not listed?
faqs.a: Because the City states no pickleball count for it. Tom Watson appears on the Racket Sports page under "Additional Tennis Courts" with the figure 4, which counts tennis courts, and nowhere in the pickleball table. The imported dataset carried twelve pickleball courts for it, and an imported number is not a stated one. The City's FAQ says new courts are scheduled to open there in spring 2026.

At the drop-in times the City prints for each gymnasium: Monday, Wednesday and Friday 7:30 to 10:30 am at North Boulder; Monday 1 to 3 pm and 6 to 8 pm and Sunday 2 to 4 pm at East Boulder; Sunday 9 to 11 am and Tuesday and Thursday 1:30 to 3:30 pm at South Boulder, with none there from June through October. Nets are not available outside those hours.
